//: Phase 7 (ADR-0019): user_project_wrapper of ChipFoundry Caravel with the Hazard3 SoC placed flat (soc_top and the SRAM directly at the wrapper level, project-plan.md §5.5). Built from pnr/soc_top/config_hazard3.json: every setting not changed below has the same value and the same reason there. Changed: the design and file list, the clock port, the die, the Caravel fixed section (caravel_user_project b510613c openlane/user_project_wrapper/config.json, 'You should NOT edit this section'), the SRAM instance and location (decision 12), the analog_io nets don't-touch for the resizer (RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_RX), and no IR supply model yet (decision 11, step 5).
//VERILOG_FILES: Exactly the source files of rtl/rtl_caravel.f (rtl/rtl_hazard3.f + rtl/caravel, checked by make lint).
//CLOCK_PORT: The SoC runs on the Wishbone clock (decision 8).
//CLOCK_PERIOD: 44 ns (user decision 2026-10-07, ADR-0004 Phase 5 addendum: with ADR-0013 the Hazard3 SoC still missed setup at max_ss_n40C by 0.381 ns, alu.funct7_32b -> regs.rdata1, harden-soc 3 at d00214d). 43 ns from 2026-10-05 (ADR-0004 Phase 3.5 addendum), 42 ns from 2026-10-04, 40 ns before. With the characterized SRAM .lib (ADR-0010) the new dout0 hold arc makes the post-CTS hold repair (0.3 ns margin) put a delay cell before rdata_q, and the sram0 dout0 half-cycle path missed setup by 0.066 ns at min_ss_n40C at 42 ns.
//FP_SIZING: Caravel fixed: the user area is 2920 x 3520 um, the pins and their positions come from the template DEF.
//VDD_NETS: Caravel fixed: the four supply pairs of the user area, each with a core ring; the logic and the SRAM use vccd1/vssd1.
//PDN_CORE_RING: Caravel fixed core ring (width 3.1, offset 12.45, spacing 1.7 um).
//MACROS: The SRAM as in soc_top; the instance is u_soc.sram0 after synthesis flattens the wrapper. Location: soc_top's (290.72, 353.6) moved about 60 um up and right to clear the core ring, in the lower-left corner near the Wishbone pins (decision 12), on the site/row grid (0.46 / 2.72 um).
//PDN_HWIDTH: met5 strap width as soc_top (decision 11, ADR-0017).
//PDN_VWIDTH: met4 strap 1.6 -> 4.8 um, the met5 width (ADR-0019 decision 18, user decision 2026-10-13). With Caravel's real supply network (one vccd1 pad and one vssd1 pad on the right side, 5 um met4 ring, met3 bridges on the left and right sides of the wrapper ring only) the worst-case IR with the block in the lower-left corner was 104.2 mV at 1.6 um, 82.2 at 3.2, 72.2 at 4.8, 66.4 at 6.4 (PDN what-if on the p7_harden2 layout): the drop is in the vertical conduction from the pad to the block, and the met4 straps carry it in parallel with Caravel's ring.
//RUN_IRDROP_REPORT: IR inside the wrapper (ADR-0019 decision 18): one supply point where each met5 strap of the net meets the left and the right side of the net's core ring, the two sides where Caravel's manual_power_connections bridges land (54 left, 53 right; no bridge on the top or bottom side). Points at the exact bridge positions crashed OpenROAD PSM (Signal 11, cause not found). 1.80 V = the nom_tt voltage of the IR step; ir_worst.py rewrites it for the ff corners. The drop from the pads through Caravel's own network is judged separately (ir_caravel.py), its limit being the board supply requirement.
//CORNERS: Fail on setup, hold and max cap in every STA corner (LibreLane's sky130 default fails setup only in tt; project-plan.md §6.2). Max slew: LibreLane's default ("": no corner fails the flow) and check_soc.py max_slew judges instead (ADR-0019 decision 16): Caravel drives la_oenb, la_data_in, wbs_adr_i and wbs_dat_i at 0.84-0.97 ns (caravel_io.sdc), above the 0.75 ns limit, which no repair inside the wrapper can change (run p7_harden2: all 384 violations on those pins and the first cells on their nets). The row allows exactly those pins, up to the Caravel transition + 0.05 ns, and fails on any other violation.
//STA_CORNERS: LibreLane's 9 sky130 corners (tt/ss/ff x nom/min/max RC) plus two for temperature inversion: at 1.60 V most cells are slower at -40 C than at 100 C (dfxtp_1 CLK->Q 11 % slower), so ss_n40C_1v60 is added, and ff_100C_1v95 for symmetry on the fast side (docs/notes/signoff_criteria_soc_top.md, Phase 4). Setting LIB replaces LibreLane's sky130 default (librelane/config/pdk_compat.py), so all five PVTs are listed. PNR_CORNERS is not set, so the other OpenROAD PnR steps (placement, global routing, STAMidPNR) use only DEFAULT_CORNER (librelane/steps/openroad.py 353-355: PNR_CORNERS or [DEFAULT_CORNER]; the variable's help text says STA_CORNERS, the code does not); the resizer uses RSZ_CORNERS and CTS uses CTS_CORNERS (unset: STA_CORNERS). Phase 5: skill multicorner-sta rule 2.
//RSZ_CORNERS: The resizer steps (RepairDesignPostGPL, ResizerTimingPostCTS, RepairDesignPostGRT) use LibreLane's 9 corners plus the three ss_n40C_1v60 corners (Phase 5, user decision 2026-10-07, ADR-0013): with only the 9, Hazard3 failed signoff setup at ss_n40C by -4.16 ns on a path with +1.48 ns at ss_100C, which the resizer judged as needing no repair; a single-step re-run of ResizerTimingPostCTS with ss_n40C added took the pre-route estimate from -7.32 to -0.21 ns (with PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN 0.1). ff_100C_1v95 stays signoff-only (soc_top: no hold violation there, Hazard3 run 2 worst +0.153 ns, PicoRV32 golden +0.087 ns). For the wrapper it was tried and rejected (ADR-0019 decision 17, user decision 2026-10-12): with the three ff_100C corners added, RepairDesignPostGRT no longer upsized 17 a221oi_1 drivers (a221oi_4 with 12 corners) and buffered behind them instead, 866 -> 4759 buffers (single-step re-run, same input, reproducible; cause not found), and global routing failed with GRT-0116, overflow 771 (run p7_harden3). The hold of the Caravel input paths at ff_100C is covered by GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN instead, and checked by signoff STA in all 15 corners.
//RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_RX: The 29 analog_io nets (unconnected inout pins of the Caravel wrapper) are don't-touch for the resizer: repair_design with global-route parasitics (RepairDesignPostGRT) counts an inout pin as both the driver and a load, and stops with [ERROR RSZ-0074] 'failed to build tree from gloubal routes: found route to 1 pins, expected 0' (OpenROAD ec354411 BufferedNet.cc makeBufferedNetGroute; RepairDesign.cc skips don't-touch nets). Run p7_harden2 step 41 stopped at analog_io[9]; a single-step re-run of the same input with this setting finished with the same repairs. check_inputs.py inout_dont_touch checks that every inout signal port of the top module matches it.
//PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN: 0.3 ns (default 0.1): the post-CTS hold repair reached +0.100 ns, but after routing the hold on sram0 input pins (SRAM .lib hold 0.5 ns: the ADR-0007 value, kept as the floor by ADR-0010; sram0 clock delayed by CTS latency balancing) fell to -0.088 ns at min_ff_n40C (Phase 4 harden-soc 2 and 3). CTS_DELAY_BUFFER_DERATE_PCT 0 or 1 did not change the 10 delay buffers of that balancing (OpenROAD CTS-0036, single-step CTS re-run), so the margin is taken in the hold repair.
//PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN: 0.1 ns (default 0.05; 0.6 until Phase 5). 0.6 stood in for ss_n40C while the resizer did not see it; with ss_n40C in RSZ_CORNERS (ADR-0013) it is not needed, and it blocked the hold repair: in the single-step re-run with 0.6 the hold repair left 21 sram0 dout0 -> rdata registers at -0.26 ns hold in ss_n40C (their setup there was at the 0.6 ns margin), with 0.1 they got their hold buffers (+0.62 ns).
//CTS_CLK_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH: 150 um: CTS buffers the wire from the clk pin to the clock tree roots (repair_clock_nets in LibreLane's cts.tcl). With the default (0, i.e. the slew-based length of about 3.5 mm) the pin at (547.6, 0.1) drove about 360 um of wire to clkbuf_regs_0_clk at (475.2, 291.0); its slew was 0.767 ns at max_ss_n40C (limit 0.75 ns; Phase 4 harden-soc 4). The pin's driver is LibreLane's assumed inv_2 (SYNTH_CLK_DRIVING_CELL default).
//STA_EXTRA_CORNER_TCL_FILE: Writes the minimum pulse width and period report of every STA corner (pulse_width.rpt). The SRAM derate of ADR-0007 is gone with the per-PVT .lib (ADR-0010): sram0 now gets the global OCV derate of base.sdc like every cell.
//PNR_SDC_FILE: pnr/user_project_wrapper/pnr.sdc: the same constraints as pnr/soc_top/pnr.sdc (base.sdc, max fanout 8, max transition 0.70, clock_uncertainty.sdc of soc_top).
//SIGNOFF_SDC_FILE: pnr/user_project_wrapper/signoff.sdc: base.sdc and soc_top's clock_uncertainty.sdc, as pnr/soc_top/signoff.sdc.
//ERROR_ON_MAGIC_DRC: Magic DRC runs on the full GDS (LibreLane default MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS = true). The SRAM's own GDS has about 4.67 million violations of the standard sky130 deck (its bitcells follow the SRAM rules), all inside the SRAM outline, so the flow must not stop on them. pnr/soc_top/check_soc.py replaces LibreLane's checker: 0 violations outside the SRAM outline and, inside it, every violation at the position of a same-rule violation of the SRAM checked alone (pnr/soc_top/sram_drc_alone.py; rule counts reviewed in signoff/waivers/soc_top/). Abstract mode (MAGIC_DRC_USE_GDS = false) was tried: it reports 416 nwell.4 errors on every standard cell row, because the abstract cell views have no taps; the full-GDS run has none. See README.md.
//PRIMARY_GDSII_STREAMOUT_TOOL: Final GDS from KLayout. Magic's GDS of this design has 13 top cells: it places the SRAM through renamed copies of its sub-cells (T2_*) and also writes the 160 original sub-cells unreferenced, so KLayout.Render failed with 'The layout has multiple top cells'. The KLayout GDS has one top cell (soc_top) and all SRAM cells are reachable from it (161 prebuilt, 169 OpenRAM self-generated; check_soc.py macro_gds compares them with the macro GDS, Phase 6). Magic still streams out; KLayout.XOR compares the two. See README.md.
//EXTRA_EXCLUDED_CELLS: Same as Phase 2 (pnr/picorv32_core/README.md): the PDK exclude list does not exclude the clkdlybuf4s25/50 delay cells, and the resizer used them as general buffers. a2111oi_1 (Phase 5, user decision 2026-10-06): the resizer resized an a2111oi_2 with an ss_100C slew violation to a2111oi_1 (it judges sizes with the first .lib read, tt), which cannot drive one clkbuf_1 within 0.49 ns in ss_100C, and RepairDesignPostGPL then inserted buffers at one point forever (92.9 GB). no_synth.cells keeps it out of synthesis only. pnr/check_weak_cells.py (check_inputs.py weak_cells) checks every cell the resizer may use; docs/notes/repair_design_loop.md. ADR-0013 (Phase 5, user decision 2026-10-07): with ss_n40C in RSZ_CORNERS, check_weak_cells.py also lists o41ai_1 (post-GPL margin 30%) and a2111oi_2, nor4b_1, a222oi_1, o311ai_1, nor4_1 (post-GRT margin 40%) at ss_n40C; EXTRA_EXCLUDED_CELLS also keeps them out of synthesis (librelane/steps/pyosys.py), which uses the larger sizes.
//CTS_SINK_CLUSTERING_SIZE: Same as Phase 2 (pnr/picorv32_core/README.md): keeps CTS leaf fanout within MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT 10.
//LAYERS_RC: Same as Phase 2 (pnr/picorv32_core/README.md): the sky130 per-layer RC table left commented out in LibreLane 3.0.14 librelane/config/pdk_compat.py lines 262-296.
//RUN_POST_GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR: Same as Phase 2 (pnr/picorv32_core/README.md): repairs slew/cap again after global routing.
//RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING: Also re-repair setup after global routing with the global-route parasitics (OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostGRT, LibreLane default false, 'experimental'; margins GRT_RESIZER_*_SLACK_MARGIN at their defaults 0.025 / 0.05 ns). ADR-0014 (user decision 2026-10-07): the post-CTS estimate was 1.24 ns more optimistic than signoff on the long Hazard3 paths at max_ss_n40C (harden 4: repair ended +0.112 ns, signoff -1.131 ns). Experiment from harden 4 after step 43 with only this switched on: signoff worst setup +0.530 ns (max_ss_n40C +0.636), hold +0.107 ns, slew/cap/fanout/route DRC/antenna 0; the step took 1 min 49 s.
//GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN: 0.2 ns (default 0.05; user decision 2026-10-12, ADR-0019 decision 17). In run p7_harden2 the post-GRT hold repair ended at +0.058 ns (its worst over RSZ_CORNERS), but after detailed routing and RCX the Caravel input path wbs_adr_i[4] -> _21509_ was -0.043 ns at max_ff_n40C, a corner the repair saw: the global-route estimate was about 0.1 ns optimistic for hold there. 0.2 covers that gap with as much again, and the ff_100C corners the resizer does not see (on this path max_ff_100C was 0.028 ns worse than max_ff_n40C; adding them to RSZ_CORNERS broke RepairDesignPostGRT, see //RSZ_CORNERS); signoff hold is still checked in all 15 corners.
//GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT: Slew margin of the repair after global routing (Phase 2: 30). Here 30 left 20 max-slew violations in the ss corners on 5 nets (run soc_explore4: 0.755-0.932 ns, 144-496 um long, driven by small cells), because the extracted wires after detailed routing load them more than the global-routing estimate. 50 made this repair run for more than 26 minutes on one thread without finishing (soc_explore6, stopped); 40 finishes in about a minute. See README.md.
//DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_SLEW_PCT: Slew margin of the repair after global placement (default 20), raised for the same reason. See README.md.
//CTS_DISTANCE_BETWEEN_BUFFERS: Same as Phase 2 (pnr/picorv32_core/README.md): buffers inside the long H-tree segments.
//PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT: Global placement target density. LibreLane's default here was 68 % while the L-shaped logic region is about half used, so cells crowd near the corner below-left of the SRAM; nets there detoured up to 3x their pin distance (soc_top run 1: 117 um apart, 353 um routed, 1.42 ns slew in ss). 55 % (soc_explore10): max slew/cap/fanout 0 in all 9 corners at 0.75 ns. See README.md. The wrapper uses 50 %: at 55 % (p7_harden5) the global routing redone after the last slew repair pushed internal net _03489_ into a detour, 0.779 ns in max_ss_n40C; at 50 % (p7_exp_pl_dens) the worst internal slew is 0.576 ns, setup +0.548 ns, hold +0.187 ns. ADR-0019 decision 21.
//DECAP_CELLS: ADR-0019 decision 24 (user decision 2026-10-14): ChipFoundry precheck klayout_met_min_ca_density checks li1.pd.1d, li1 at most 60 % of the area in 235/4 (the 2920 x 3520 um wrapper). With the PDK default (sky130_fd_sc_hd__decap_3, 87 % li1) Fill Insertion put 2,461,688 decap_3 in the empty wrapper (9.24 mm2) and li1 was 75 % (run f4ea9de); the 2.46 million instances also took KLayout BEOL and Magic extraction (LVS, OEB) over the 10 GiB of the precheck VM. sky130_ef_sc_hd__decap_12 has 52 % li1 (fd decap_12: 97 %; fill: 12.5 %), estimate 50 %; its LEF and SPICE are already in the flow, it has no .lib. The precheck deck finds nothing on an array of it with fill_2/fill_1 (docs/notes/caravel_precheck_phase7.md section 10). caravel_user_project turns fill insertion off, but its wrapper has macros only.
//FILL_CELLS: With 12-site decaps, fill_8 and fill_4 fill the gaps in fewer instances than fill_2 / fill_1 alone (the PDK default).
//DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH: Splits nets longer than 200 um with buffers in the repair before CTS. Without it (run soc_explore2): 48 nets on SRAM inputs up to 355 um long (the SRAM LEF has no antenna data, so they are not antenna-checked), 50 max-slew violations in the ss corners (up to 1.09 ns on nets of about 300-700 um), and 7 max-fanout violations from antenna repair putting 10-11 diodes on single long nets. The same limit after global routing (GRT_DESIGN_REPAIR_MAX_WIRE_LENGTH 200) is not set: run soc_explore3 with it stopped with GRT-0229 'Vertical edge usage exceeds the maximum allowed. (79, 0) usage=65534' at the clk pin, but that error was later found to happen at random in OpenROAD.RepairDesignPostGRT without it too (2 of 4 re-runs of the same step; pnr/librelane_flow.sh retries it), so whether the setting matters is not known; 400 um changed nothing (run soc_explore9). See README.md.
